scenarios: a server proposed for the site's origin is untrusted: the page read says so and why, and the protected action runs through the interface (the M7.4 fallback) with the host recording the click

once a person trusts it the page read prefers the site's tool by name, the same action is refused SITE_TOOL_PREFERRED and the host is never asked to click anything, and the order is placed through external.call instead
a server is bound to an exact origin: a different scheme or port is not the same site
proof: one cart page and one protected button, with the trust decision in between; the fake host's record of what it was asked to click is the evidence of which rung the host took.
audit: PARTIAL before: rungs 2-4 built and proven in M7; nothing bound a server to an origin and browser.act knew of no better path.
limitations: only a protected action prefers the site tool; no entity-to-tool mapping; origins match exactly; the kernel judges the class before the effector, so an approval is asked before the refusal.
